opportunities.title: Propose vulnerability identity key and lifecycle schema
opportunities.summary: ### Summary Inspect the committed Anchore JSON fixtures and propose a schema for tracking vulnerabilities over time. Specifically: what combination of fields uniquely identifies "the same vulnerability" across scans? Candidates to evaluate include CVE ID alone, CVE + package name, CVE + package name + version, and CVE + package + image. Write up the tradeoffs, pick a recommendation, and sketch the analytics DB table(s) needed to support first_seen / last_seen / fixed_at / ignored_at / cleared_at fields. **Tech notes:** The Anchore JSON schema is documented at the Anchore project site; worth skimming before diving into fixtures. The goal of this spike is a decision, not code — resist the urge to start implementing. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Written proposal (markdown doc in PR) covering identity key options, tradeoffs, and a recommendation - [ ] Proposed analytics DB schema with column types and rationale - [ ] At least one worked example from the fixtures showing how the identity key behaves across days - [ ] Reviewed and approved by Brandon and/or Matt before next ticket starts ## Bounty: $250 This issue has been selected for our paid contributor program. opportunities.title: [Add] TON: gasless transfers via W5 relayer — pay fees in USDT (revenue line) [TON / Gasless]
opportunities.summary: **What:** Gasless TON transfers — users pay fees in the token they're sending (USDT etc.) instead of needing native TON. **This is a revenue line, not just UX:** the user signs a batch containing their transfer plus a fee payment to our relayer; the relayer (VultiServer is the natural host) broadcasts, pays the native gas, and keeps the in-token fee. Phantom charges ~1.5% for the equivalent on Solana; Tonkeeper monetizes via Battery. **Why users expect it:** "Can't send my $2,000 USDT because I have no TON" is the top wallet-switching complaint in the TON ecosystem; Tonkeeper and Telegram Wallet both ship it. **How it works with our vaults:** the relayer is broadcast-side only — it never joins the key ceremony. Fast and secure vaults sign the same W5 batch; the relayer can't alter it (signature covers the batch), worst case it declines to broadcast. Non-custodial throughout. **Depends on:** W5 wallet contract support (#2181's W5 item) — gasless is a W5 feature. Revenue/parity item under epic #2181.
opportunities.eligibilityReason: Payout evidence is below the bootstrap confidence threshold.

opportunities.summary: `source.md` contains the complete RFC 5322 specification (Internet Message Format). We need a **fully conformant email address parser** in Python that implements the complete ABNF grammar from sections 3.2 through 3.4, plus obsolete syntax from §4.4. opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
